scope: execution only: the tasks, sets, searches, proposer, budget, measures, hypotheses, and analyses are unchanged
observation: For the run's first two hours keys-v0.1 ran ten Lean REPL workers beside this run's eight and the model server, and the Windows commit limit ran out (at 01:55 local time 8.0 GB of commit free with 34.6 GB of physical memory free; a Python process failed to allocate 4.4 MB and a Lean build stopped with 'INTERNAL PANIC: out of memory'). Of the 672 rows recorded by then, 127 searches were not constructed without a reason (the session produced no task), 15 were not constructed because the declaration range was not found, and 7 were abandoned by a REPL timeout during setup, after 0.3 to 28 seconds; in 31 units one or two searches were not constructed while another search of the same unit, on the same task, was. A search that is not constructed is left out of every comparison, and an abandoned one counts as not proving its theorem, so such failures are not a property of the search.
change: run_search_coupled.run_all treats a unit as unfinished, once, when one of its rows is not constructed for a reason other than a missing declaration range, or is abandoned by a REPL timeout: a resume runs all three searches of that unit again, set 0 with its seeded draws and sets 1 and 2 with fresh draws, as for a unit that raised, and the unit's new rows replace the old. It applies to every unit, whatever its outcome, and a unit that fails again keeps its second rows. The resume is made after the current run finishes, with no other REPL workers on the machine.
resultsSeenBeforeAmendment: the runner's progress lines (per unit: expansions, whether a proof was found, draws, errors) were read while diagnosing, and the operational counts above were computed from the recorded rows; no summary, rate, comparison, or hypothesis was computed
